subject.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content

question: Should this PR land as a forward-only QMD adapter fix while existing short-term recall records remain untouched, or must memory-core provide an upgrade repair before release?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but repository policy treats persistent state upgrades as an owner decision and the correct migration or discard lifecycle cannot be inferred safely from the adapter patch alone.

options.title: Land and track cleanup
options.body: Merge the adapter fix after rebasing and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106937 open for a narrow memory-core-owned historical recall cleanup.

options.title: Require cleanup before merge
options.body: Extend this work with a tested memory-core doctor or repair path that removes or normalizes contaminated persisted recalls before users encounter mixed old and new state.

options.title: Pause for state design
options.body: Hold the PR until the owner chooses whether contaminated recall state should be migrated, selectively repaired, or safely discarded and rebuilt.

recommendation.title: Land and track cleanup
recommendation.body: Merge the adapter fix after rebasing and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106937 open for a narrow memory-core-owned historical recall cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior QMD line-range and memory behavior work is closest to both the adapter semantics and the persisted-state compatibility choice.
